Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our formal security intake we need a few items to close the vendor security review (internal ticket: NOV-SR-1198):

1) SIG questionnaire answers (or CAIQ mapping) — key controls around encryption, key management, and incident response.
2) Full subprocessor inventory with residency (country), purpose, access scope, and whether they have KMS access.
3) Evidence for KMS residency (who manages keys, which regions, HSM/KMS vendor, and any attestations).

Can you confirm a target delivery date? If you can share a short plan (what you'll deliver and when) we can align with procurement.

Also attaching our intake checklist (referenced) — we'll expect answers in the CAIQ format if possible.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — that timeline looks reasonable. A few items we need called out explicitly in the CAIQ mapping:

- KMS / key custody model: does Redwood manage keys for hosted customers or do customers bring their own? We need to know which keys (system vs. customer) are in which region.
- Any transitive subprocessors that may have key material access (e.g., logging/backup vendors, analytics buckets).
- Dataflow diagram or short narrative showing where customer data passes through Redwood and which subprocessors can see plaintext.

Procurement also asked for a short statement describing your retention of subprocessor evidence (how long you'll keep subprocessor attestation artifacts).

If you can add those to the Thu draft we'll review and send any redlines back.

Aisha / procurement team —

Thanks for the patience. Per our plan, attached are the first-pass deliverables for your review:

1) redwood_subprocessor_inventory_v2.csv — our current roster with country, purpose, and KMS-access flag.
2) redwood_caic_mapping_draft.pdf — CAIQ mapping draft with answers to the encryption/KMS/IR controls you called out.
3) kms_residency_statement_20270620.pdf — signed statement describing key custody model and regional residency; indicates Redwood manages system keys and customers may optionally bring their own KMS via our Private deployment.

Notes/assumptions included in the CAIQ draft: we flagged transitive logging vendors that process encrypted blobs only (no plaintext access) and called out backup vendors that can access decrypted snapshots per customer config (these are optional and appear in the CSV).

Retention: we retain subprocessor attestation materials and evidence for 3 years by default; copies tied to contract renewal are archived per request. If procurement needs a longer retention window let us know and we can propose an addendum.

Next steps: please send any redlines on the CAIQ mapping by Thu 2027-06-24 so we can finalize the evidence bundle. If procurement requires a notarized KMS attestation we'll escalate to Legal for signature routing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
